**Sang K. Oh, President and Chief Executive Officer:**


“We delivered solid results in the third quarter, with net income of $7.8 million and diluted EPS of $0.52. Continued loan growth supported higher net interest income and further expansion in net interest margin. Book value per share continued to increase, reflecting growth in shareholders’ equity, while we maintained appropriate capital levels. As we enter the final quarter of 2026, we remain committed to sustainable growth, disciplined risk management and operating efficiency,” said Sang K. Oh, President and Chief Executive Officer.

***Third Quarter 2026 vs. Second Quarter 2026***


Net interest income increased by $2.1 million, or 11%, primarily driven by continued loan growth and the normalization of Federal Reserve Bank account income following a prior-quarter accrual adjustment. These benefits were partially offset by higher interest expense resulting from growth in average interest-bearing deposit balances. As a result, net interest margin increased by 19 basis points to 3.27%.


- **Interest-bearing Deposits in Other Banks** : Interest income increased by $1.1 million, primarily reflecting the absence of a one-time Federal Reserve Bank accrual adjustment recorded in the prior quarter, as well as higher average balances.
- **Loans** : Interest income increased by $1.9 million, driven largely by an $80.9 million or 4% increase in average loan balances, reflecting growth in CRE and home mortgage loans, along with a 5-basis-point increase in average loan yield to 6.41%.
- **Deposits** : Interest expense increased by $1.0 million, primarily due to a $76.4 million or 4% increase in average interest-bearing deposit balances, including growth in money market and time deposit accounts. Despite the higher balances, the average cost of interest-bearing deposits increased only 2 basis points to 3.79%, reflecting relatively stable funding costs during the quarter.


***Third Quarter 2026 vs. Third Quarter 2025***


Net interest income increased by $1.9 million, or 9%, primarily driven by balance sheet growth and lower deposit rates. These favorable factors were partially offset by lower loan yields. As a result, the net interest margin increased by one basis point to 3.27%.


- **Loans** : Interest income increased by $2.6 million, largely attributable to a $201.9 million increase in average loan balances, reflecting continued growth in CRE loans. The increase was partially offset by an 11-basis-point decline in loan yields, reflecting the impact of the federal funds rate cuts during the prior year and the repricing of adjustable-rate loans and newly originated loans.
- **Deposits** : Interest expense increased by $463 thousand, mainly due to a $173.3 million increase in average interest-bearing deposit balances, driven mainly by growth in time deposits. The increase was partially offset by a 28-basis-point decline in costs of interest-bearing deposits, reflecting the repricing of time deposits and money market accounts following the federal funds rate cuts.

***Third Quarter 2026 vs. Second Quarter 2026***


Noninterest income decreased by $356 thousand, or 6%, primarily driven by lower other income.


- **Gains on Sale of Loans** : Decreased by $93 thousand, primarily reflecting a lower average premium rate, partially offset by higher SBA loan sales volume. The Bank sold $51.1 million in SBA loans at an average premium rate of 8.06%, compared with $49.1 million sold at an average premium rate of 8.17% in the prior period.
- **Other Income** : Decreased by $222 thousand, mainly due to higher unrealized losses on CRA mutual funds from higher market interest rates.


***Third Quarter 2026 vs. Third Quarter 2025***


Noninterest income increased by $1.2 million, or 28%, primarily due to higher gains on sale of loans.


- **Gains on Sale of Loans:** Increased by $1.2 million, driven by stronger SBA loan sale activity and higher premium rates. The Bank sold $51.1 million in SBA loans at an average premium rate of 8.06%, compared with $36.8 million sold at an average premium rate of 6.71% in the prior period.

Noninterest expense increased by $686 thousand, or 5%, primarily due to higher professional fees.


- **Professional Fees** : Increased by $675 thousand, primarily due to higher non-recurring legal and professional service expenses incurred during the quarter.


***Third Quarter 2026 vs. Third Quarter 2025***


Noninterest expense increased by $1.9 million, or 14%, primarily due to higher professional fees and salaries and employee benefits.


- **Salaries and Employee Benefits** : Increased by $560 thousand, primarily due to staffing growth, annual salary adjustments effective April 2026, and higher incentive accruals associated with increased SBA loan production.
- **Professional Fees** : Increased by $710 thousand, primarily due to higher non-recurring legal and professional service expenses compared to the prior year.


**Income Tax Expense**


***Third Quarter 2026 vs. Second Quarter 2026***


Income tax expense decreased by $434 thousand to $2.6 million, primarily due to lower pre-tax income and a lower effective tax rate. The effective tax rate decreased to 25.3% from 27.8%, primarily due to return-to-provision adjustments associated with the prior-year tax returns.


***Third Quarter 2026 vs. Third Quarter 2025***


Income tax expense decreased by $339 thousand to $2.6 million, primarily reflecting a lower effective tax rate, partially offset by higher pre-tax income. The effective tax rate decreased to 25.3% from 30.7%, mainly due to the absence of a one-time deferred tax asset revaluation recognized in the prior-year period and return-to-provision adjustments associated with the prior-year tax returns.

- Nonperforming loans increased by $768 thousand, primarily driven by $2.2 million of loans migrating into nonaccrual status, partially offset by a $1.1 million decrease in the balances of existing nonperforming loans.
- Criticized loans increased by $44.1 million, primarily driven by $45.7 million of loans newly entering the category during the quarter. The new additions were primarily CRE loans rated Special Mention.
- Special Mention loans increased by $42.9 million, primarily driven by four relationships totaling $41.5 million. An $8.2 million C&I relationship and a $5.9 million CRE relationship were downgraded primarily due to DCR covenant shortfalls but remain current. A $6.2 million CRE loan is in early delinquency due to sponsor liquidity constraints, while a $21.3 million CRE developer relationship in downtown Los Angeles remains current and performing, with the property being marketed for sale. Management continues to closely monitor these relationships and believes there is a viable path toward a positive resolution through repayment or credit upgrades over the next few quarters.

**ABOUT OP BANCORP**


OP Bancorp, the holding company for Open Bank (the “Bank”), is a California corporation whose common stock is quoted on the Nasdaq Global Market under the ticker symbol, “OPBK.” The Bank operates a general commercial banking business in Los Angeles, Orange, and Santa Clara Counties in California, the Dallas metropolitan area in Texas, and Clark County in Nevada, serving small- and medium-sized businesses, professionals, and local residents with a particular focus on Korean and other Asian communities. The Bank currently operates twelve full-service branch offices in Downtown Los Angeles, Los Angeles Fashion District, Los Angeles Koreatown, Cerritos, Gardena, Buena Park, Garden Grove and Santa Clara, California, Carrollton, Texas and Las Vegas, Nevada. The Bank also has one loan production office in Bellevue, Washington. The Bank commenced its operations on June 10, 2005 as First Standard Bank and changed its name to Open Bank in October 2010. Its headquarters is located at 1000 Wilshire Blvd., Suite 500, Los Angeles, California 90017.
